name: CNCF Platforms White Paper
claim: A platform curates capabilities for internal users, should hide implementation complexity behind consistent interfaces, and should be evolved as a product around user outcomes.
scope_limit: Guidance for internal cloud platforms; it does not define data-product or lakehouse semantic boundaries.

name: Martin Fowler: Bounded Context
summary: Evidence that language/model boundaries are not necessarily product packaging.
claim: Bounded contexts establish a consistent model and language within a boundary and require explicit mappings across boundaries.
scope_limit: Explains semantic/model boundaries, not a complete product identity test.

name: Thoughtworks: Designing data products
summary: Use-case, ownership and SLO evidence for data-product boundaries.
claim: Data-product boundaries should be worked backward from use cases, generalized across additional use cases, assigned one domain owner and given SLOs.
scope_limit: A practitioner method for data products, not a universal software-product ontology.

name: ISO/IEC 25010:2023
claim: ICT product quality must be specified and evaluated through a product lifecycle and may include software, data, infrastructure and other components.
scope_limit: The public abstract does not expose all normative quality subcharacteristics or define portfolio boundaries.

name: The Open Group IT4IT Reference Architecture
claim: Digital products require end-to-end lifecycle and value-stream management rather than build-only decomposition.
scope_limit: IT management reference architecture; it does not enumerate data-and-analytics products.

name: DAMA-DMBOK core knowledge areas
claim: Data management spans governance, architecture, modelling, storage/operations, security, integration, content, master/reference data, warehousing/BI, metadata and quality.
scope_limit: Knowledge areas are disciplines, not automatically products or bounded contexts.

name: Apache Iceberg Table Specification
claim: An analytical table format separately specifies immutable files, table metadata, snapshots, manifests, schema/partition evolution and atomic metadata replacement, while expecting a catalog to supply/manage table location.
scope_limit: One open table format; alternatives and features beyond adopted editions require separate evidence.

name: Apache Iceberg REST Catalog Specification
claim: The REST catalog protocol separates catalog interactions from engine implementations to support language and engine interoperability.
scope_limit: Protocol scope does not by itself define all catalog management, governance or enterprise metadata semantics.

name: Apache Polaris
summary: Independent catalog implementation and multi-engine evidence.
claim: An open catalog can implement the Iceberg REST API and interoperate with multiple independent query and processing engines.
scope_limit: One catalog project and table ecosystem; it is implementation evidence rather than semantic authority for the entire portfolio.

name: Apache Polaris API Specifications
summary: Evidence that catalog and management/policy APIs are separable surfaces.
claim: Polaris publishes separate management APIs and catalog APIs, including principals, roles, catalogs, generic tables, notifications and policy surfaces.
scope_limit: Project-specific extensions do not automatically become universal catalog semantics.

name: OpenLineage
claim: Lineage metadata can be collected through a standard extensible event model for datasets, jobs and runs across multiple pipeline components.
scope_limit: Runtime lineage is not statistical causality, business truth or complete provenance by itself.

name: Local data-platform DDD model
claim: The existing model separates source estate, contracts, products/assets, ingestion, transformation, orchestration, quality, lineage, metrics, machines, compilation, runtime, decision, governance, reliability and control contexts.
scope_limit: Structurally validated local research candidate; not independently reviewed, ratified or product-boundary complete.

name: External 99 DAT library prose candidate
claim: The report proposes 99 provider-neutral DAT semantic libraries and explicitly keeps compiler, runtime, resource, control, assurance and client-facing responsibilities outside DAT ownership.
scope_limit: Only prose is present; referenced registry, generator, validator and archive were not supplied or independently verified.
